premises.title: The Sundered Crown
premises.logline: The old king's crown was broken into three and buried apart for good reason. {villain} has found the first piece.

objective.why: Reforged, the crown commands every soul buried under the border forts.
objective.ifLost: {villain} wears a crown of bone, and four centuries of dead soldiers stand up at once.

clock.label: The Crown Reforged
clock.onFill: The third shard is set. The barrow-line wakes.

premises.title: The Drowning Bell
premises.logline: A bell no one can find rings under the water every night, and each time it does, {region} loses another mile of coast.

objective.why: Three anchors were sunk to hold the bell silent. Two have already been cut loose.
objective.ifLost: The bell rings without stopping and the water takes the harbour towns in a single night.

clock.label: The Water Rises
clock.onFill: The last anchor parts. High tide never goes out again.

premises.title: The Long Winter
premises.logline: Winter came early to {region} and has not moved since. Something is holding it in place on purpose.

objective.why: Three embers were carried out of the first fire. Rekindled together, they break any season held by force.
objective.ifLost: The frost line reaches the lowlands and does not stop at the sea.

clock.label: The Deepening Frost
clock.onFill: The last road out of {region} closes under forty feet of snow.

premises.title: The Hollow Succession
premises.logline: The heir to {region} died three months ago. Someone is still wearing them, and the coronation is in six weeks.

objective.why: Three pieces of evidence, taken together, unmake the impostor in front of witnesses who matter.
objective.ifLost: The crown is placed on a thing that is not a person, and every noble house signs its name under it.

clock.label: Days to the Coronation
clock.onFill: The coronation proceeds. The court belongs to {villain}.

premises.title: The Green Flood
premises.logline: The forest has crossed the old boundary stones for the first time in nine hundred years, and it is not stopping at the fields.

objective.why: Three stones still stand. Re-cut and re-sworn, they hold the treaty line.
objective.ifLost: The treaty is void. Everything built inside the old wood goes back to the wood.

clock.label: The Wood Advances
clock.onFill: The last boundary stone is swallowed. {hub} has three days.

premises.title: The Ash Covenant
premises.logline: A contract signed a hundred years ago is being called in, and the collectors have started at the smallest villages in {region}.

objective.why: Three seals authenticate the contract. Break them and the whole covenant is unenforceable.
objective.ifLost: The debt is collected in full. Every soul named in the ledger is carried off on the same night.

clock.label: The Ledger Closes
clock.onFill: The account is settled. {hub} is empty by morning.

premises.title: The Wyrm's Tithe
premises.logline: {villain} has begun taking a tithe from {region}: first gold, then livestock, and this season, people.

objective.why: Three neighbouring powers each hold a token of the old alliance. Bring them together and there is an army instead of a rout.
objective.ifLost: {region} pays the tithe every season forever, and the price only goes up.

clock.label: The Next Tithe
clock.onFill: The tithe is collected. {hub} loses a generation.

premises.title: The Quiet Plague
premises.logline: People in {region} are not dying. They are forgetting, a little more each week, and something is eating what they lose.
themes: what a place is without its memory

objective.why: Three objects still hold true memory of what is being erased. They are the only evidence that will survive.
objective.ifLost: Nobody in {region} can remember there was ever anything wrong.

clock.label: The Forgetting
clock.onFill: {hub} forgets its own name, and the maps go blank.

premises.title: The Iron Road
premises.logline: An army is marching a road that was not there last spring, and it runs straight through {region} to something older than the war.

objective.why: The road is held down by three nails driven at its bends. Pull them and the road unmakes itself.
objective.ifLost: The road reaches the gate it was built for, and what is behind that gate comes out.

clock.label: The Column Advances
clock.onFill: The vanguard reaches the gate at the road's end.

premises.title: The Buried Star
premises.logline: Something fell in {region} a long time ago and was covered over carefully. The digging started again this spring.
themes: some doors were shut for us

objective.why: Three keys turn the seal. All three must turn, and only from the outside.
objective.ifLost: The seal opens from the inside instead, and {region} is the first thing it sees.

clock.label: The Dig Deepens
clock.onFill: The excavation reaches the hull, and the light goes wrong for sixty miles.

objectiveKinds.label: Recover the scattered
objectiveKinds.frame: {count} {objects} are out there, apart, and whoever holds all of them decides how this ends.
objectiveKinds.playerGoal: Find the {objects} before {villain} does, and keep them out of their hands.
objectiveKinds.failure: {villain} holds every {object} and uses them as intended.
tokenNotes: Held in the deepest room, and its keeper knows exactly what it is.
Hidden in plain sight and mislabelled; the party will walk past it once.
Already being moved when the party arrives, which is the whole encounter.

objectiveKinds.label: Break what the plan rests on
objectiveKinds.frame: {villain}'s work stands on {count} {objects}. None of them can be carried away, but all of them can be broken.
objectiveKinds.playerGoal: Get to the {objects} and destroy them, before {villain} finishes what they are for.
objectiveKinds.failure: The last {object} holds, the rite completes on schedule, and nobody was in the room to stop it.
tokenNotes: Too heavy and too fixed to move; breaking it is loud, slow, and witnessed.
Breaking it releases what it was holding, which is a problem for the next ten minutes.
It can be broken from here or disabled properly from somewhere deeper, and only one of those lasts.

objectiveKinds.label: Prove it in public
objectiveKinds.frame: Everyone suspects. Nobody can prove it. {count} pieces of {objects} exist, and each one alone is deniable.
objectiveKinds.playerGoal: Gather proof that will stand up in front of people with the power to act, and get it in front of them intact.
objectiveKinds.failure: The case never comes together, the accusation is laughed out of the room, and {villain} is owed an apology.
tokenNotes: A document, and it is worthless without the person who can swear to it.
A witness rather than an object: they have to survive to the end to matter.
Physical, damning, and currently sitting in someone else's evidence room.

objectiveKinds.label: Hold what they want
objectiveKinds.frame: There is one {object}, the party has it or is standing in front of it, and {villain} is going to keep coming.
objectiveKinds.playerGoal: Keep the {object} out of {villain}'s hands. You will not get to choose the ground.
objectiveKinds.failure: It is taken, in the end, and everything after is about what {villain} does with it.
tokenNotes: It cannot be hidden, only moved, and moving it is when they come.
Someone in the party's own circle has already been offered a great deal of money for it.

objectiveKinds.label: Get it there
objectiveKinds.frame: One {object} has to reach the far side of {region}, and every road there is watched.
objectiveKinds.playerGoal: Get the {object} to where it is going, in one piece, with the people carrying it still alive.
objectiveKinds.failure: It never arrives, and the people waiting for it make their own arrangements.
tokenNotes: Heavy, awkward, and impossible to explain at a checkpoint.
It has opinions about where it is going, and it is not shy about them.

objectiveKinds.label: Pull down the pillars
objectiveKinds.frame: {villain} cannot be beaten in a straight fight, but they stand on {count} {objects}, and those can be taken away one at a time.
objectiveKinds.playerGoal: Take away what holds {villain} up, until they can be reached at all.
objectiveKinds.failure: The support holds, and the party never gets within a mile of {villain}.
tokenNotes: It is a person, an alliance, or a debt, and it can be broken by turning it rather than killing it.
Removing it publicly is worth twice what removing it quietly is.
It will not break; it can only be bought, and the price is real.

objectiveKinds.label: Get out
objectiveKinds.frame: The way out of {region} is shut in {count} places, and {villain} would rather nobody left to talk about it.
objectiveKinds.playerGoal: Open the road out and get everyone who wants to leave through it.
objectiveKinds.failure: The way stays shut. Whatever happens in {region} stays in {region}, which is exactly the point.
tokenNotes: A pass, a gate, or a bridge, held by people who were told why.
It opens from the far side, which is a problem to be solved rather than a door to be picked.
It is not locked so much as watched, and the watchers are not the difficulty.

objectiveKinds.label: Get them to agree
objectiveKinds.frame: {count} powers each hold part of what is needed, and none of them will move while the others are in the room.
objectiveKinds.playerGoal: Get three parties who despise each other to agree to one thing, in writing, before it stops mattering.
objectiveKinds.failure: The talks collapse, everyone goes home armed, and {villain} deals with them one at a time.
tokenNotes: They will sign if the party does something for them first, and it is not a small thing.
They will sign only if a particular other party is humiliated on the way.
They have already signed something else, with {villain}, and are hoping nobody checks.

wardThreats: A quiet approach: someone the party half-trusts asks to carry it, just for the crossing.
A crowd, a jostle, and hands that know exactly where it is kept.
An open attempt in daylight, by people who expected the party to be somewhere else.
Not a theft: an offer, generous enough that refusing it makes an enemy.
They take a hostage instead and name their price in the same breath.
A fire, a flood, or a collapse, aimed at making the party choose what to carry out.
Someone official arrives with paperwork demanding it be surrendered, and the paperwork is real.
They do not come at all, which is worse, because it means they know where it will be tomorrow.

necromancer.label: necromancer
goals: to finish a resurrection that was interrupted a century ago
to prove that death is an administrative error and correct it
to raise an army that never needs feeding, then present the bill
methods: opening old battlefields and pressing what is under them into service
buying corpses through a shell company of undertakers
seeding graveyards with a slow contagion of animation
resources: a charter house of grave-robbers
three barrow-fields already emptied
a ledger of every burial in {region} for two hundred years
weaknesses: the anchoring phylactery is hidden but immobile
the binding on their servants is spoken aloud, and can be answered aloud
they cannot bear to destroy a record, even an incriminating one
lieutenants: a wight who was a magistrate and still holds court
a mortician who prepares the risen and hates them
a child-shaped thing that carries the ledger

cult_leader.label: cult leader
titles: the Voice of the Ninth Hour
goals: to complete a rite that has needed eight hundred participants and finally has them
to bring their patron partway into the world, feet first
to be the last person their god ever has to speak to
methods: converting the desperate faster than the region can replace them
buying up shrines and quietly changing what is worshipped in them
staging miracles that cost exactly one life each
resources: a congregation that includes the town watch
a shrine network across four settlements
a patron that answers, sometimes
weaknesses: the rite requires their voice, so silence them and it stalls
half the congregation is coerced, not converted
their patron is impatient and punishes delay
lieutenants: a former inquisitor who converted mid-interrogation
a smiling almoner who buys children's silence with bread
the celebrant who has read further than they were meant to

warlord.label: warlord
goals: to take and hold {region} before the spring thaw makes it defensible
to force a border that no treaty will be able to argue with
to build the state that exiled them a rival they cannot ignore
methods: taking the granaries first and the walls later
hiring every free company within a hundred miles
making examples of exactly one settlement per month
resources: four companies of drilled infantry
a siege train moving slower than the rumours about it
a quartermaster who has never lost a supply column
weaknesses: the army is loyal to pay, not to them
their supply line crosses one bridge
they will not refuse a formal challenge in front of their officers
lieutenants: a scout captain who is quietly negotiating with the other side
a siege engineer who loves the work more than the cause
a standard-bearer who believes every word

dragon_tyrant.label: dragon
goals: to formalise a protection racket into an actual sovereignty
to grow the hoard past the point where anyone could buy them out
to be owed something by every living thing in {region}
methods: taxing through intermediaries who take the blame
burning one holding a season as a demonstration
cultivating a client aristocracy that depends on them
resources: a lair no army has found
a network of kobold assessors and clerks
two noble houses already in their pocket
weaknesses: vanity, and an inability to let an insult stand
a hoard-item they will abandon a battle to protect
they honour the exact letter of a bargain even when it ruins them
lieutenants: a human factor who does the collecting and the lying
a kobold archivist with the whole ledger memorised
a knight who lost and now serves

fey_bargainer.label: fey power
goals: to collect on a promise made by people three generations dead
to move the boundary of their court a few miles further every year
to be given, freely, the one thing they cannot simply take
methods: offering exactly what each person most wants, at a price paid later
twisting old local customs into binding contract law
making the seasons a negotiating position
resources: every crossroads oath sworn in {region} for a century
a court that finds the whole affair delightful
the ability to be somewhere else instantly
weaknesses: they cannot lie outright, only mislead
iron, salt, and a guest-right honoured properly
their true name, written down by someone who was there
lieutenants: a mortal steward who has been sixteen for forty years
a hag who handles the paperwork and enjoys it
a knight of thorns bound by a promise they regret

aberrant_mind.label: aberration
goals: to finish thinking a thought that requires the whole region as scratch paper
to make a place where its rules apply instead of the ones already here
to be understood, once, by anything at all
methods: editing what people remember rather than what they do
spreading through wells, dreams, and shared meals
recruiting brilliant people by answering their favourite question
resources: a population that no longer trusts its own recollection
thralls in every trade including the temple
geometry that does not agree with the map
weaknesses: it does not understand deception performed badly on purpose
its influence thins in running water and in daylight
one thrall was left deliberately unedited, as a control
lieutenants: a physician who has been prescribing the contagion
a cartographer redrawing the region to match
a thrall who is aware and cannot say so

devil_broker.label: infernal broker
goals: to call in a century-old covenant on schedule and under budget
to establish enforceable infernal contract law in a mortal jurisdiction
to earn a promotion measured in souls per quarter
methods: buying debts nobody else wants and consolidating them
arranging accidents that are technically breaches of contract
hiring mortal lawyers who are very good and completely unaware
resources: a chain of signed instruments going back four generations
a compliant magistrate
an office nobody can find twice
weaknesses: a genuine procedural error voids the instrument
they must state the terms truthfully when asked directly
they cannot break their own contract, even to win
lieutenants: a mortal solicitor with excellent handwriting
an imp that handles filing and blackmail
a repentant co-signatory who wants out

giant_king.label: giant lord
goals: to prove a claim in the old giant order and climb back up it
to take back the high country by the measure their people used to use
to make the small folk part of the accounting again
methods: breaking the passes one at a time
demanding tribute measured in an obsolete and impossible unit
settling disputes personally and permanently
resources: a hold above the snowline
beasts that will not be turned by cavalry
a claim that other giants take seriously
weaknesses: bound by an oath-form they will not break in front of kin
the hold has one supply route
they underestimate anything smaller than a bear
lieutenants: a runecarver who does not believe in the claim
a human interpreter and hostage
a younger kin waiting for a mistake

doppelganger_ring.label: conspiracy
goals: to replace enough of {region}'s officials that replacement stops being necessary
to inherit a legitimate government rather than overthrow one
to make one specific person's signature theirs
methods: substitution, slowly, starting with people nobody visits
keeping the originals alive somewhere as reference
letting the real institutions do the actual work
resources: seats on the council
the originals, in a cellar, catalogued
an alibi for everyone
weaknesses: the copies share information poorly and imperfectly
a detail of the original's habits they never get right
the originals are kept alive, and can be found
lieutenants: a copy who prefers the borrowed life to their own
the handler who assigns the faces
an original who was turned rather than replaced

an old military road going the wrong way

a glacier with a road under it

funnel_to_hub.label: Funnel to hub
funnel_to_hub.note: A tight scripted opening, a settlement to breathe in, independent spokes, then the climax.

gated_sandbox.label: Gated sandbox
gated_sandbox.note: One region, no exit. The locations are fixed, the objectives float across them.

hub_and_spoke.label: Hub and spoke
hub_and_spoke.note: A settlement at the centre and independent missions radiating out. Forgiving of absent players.

branch_reconverge.label: Branch and reconverge
branch_reconverge.note: Three routes to the same climax. Real agency without three times the prep.

hexcrawl_mega.label: Hexcrawl plus megadungeon
hexcrawl_mega.note: Procedural travel and attrition feeding one very large site.

act_structure.label: Act structure
act_structure.note: Chronological acts rather than places. Urban, factional, intrigue-driven.

node_investigation.label: Node investigation
node_investigation.note: A clue graph. The order emerges from play; every conclusion has three ways in.

linear.label: Linear
linear.note: Chapter one to the end, no branching. Short, tightly plotted, easy to run.

one_shot.label: One shot
one_shot.note: A single sitting: a hook that lands in the first ten minutes, one location worth exploring, and a confrontation that settles it before the night is out.

dungeonKinds.label: Vault / Tomb
approaches: The hillside opens in a stepped shaft, and the steps go down further than the light does. Someone has cleared the brush from the doorway recently, and not with a blade.
Cut stones lie tumbled where the barrow's face has slumped in. Cold air comes up out of the gap, steady as breath, smelling of dry dust.
Grave markers stand in rows that stop well short of the entrance, as though whoever set them would come no closer.
origins: raised over the barrow of a king whose name was struck out
cut as a prison and re-consecrated as a grave
built by a guild that buried its own secrets with its masters

dungeonKinds.label: Lair
approaches: The trail narrows to a game path, and the game path ends at a hole in the rock. Bones lie scattered at the opening, cracked lengthwise and picked clean.
The cave mouth is low and wet. The ground in front of it has been beaten flat by something that comes and goes on all fours, and the smell reaches you before the dark does.
Flies find you before the entrance does. Whatever lives here has been eating well, and has not been tidy about it.
origins: a natural cave enlarged by something with claws
an old cellar the country grew over
a hollow under a fallen god-statue

dungeonKinds.label: Ruin
approaches: Walls stand waist high and no higher, mapping out rooms the roof gave up on centuries ago. Only one stair still runs down, and it has been swept.
The place has been picked over: fresh scratches on the stone, a rope still tied off at the lip, boot prints that have not yet weathered.
What is left above ground is only a suggestion. The real building is underneath, and the way in is a gap where a floor gave way.
motifs: ivy that grows the wrong direction
origins: a monastery abandoned in a single night
a manor that burned with the family inside
an outpost that lost its war quietly

dungeonKinds.label: Stronghold
approaches: The gate is shut, but the wall beside it is not. The breach is old and its edges are fire blackened. Nothing moves on the battlements, which is not the same as nothing watching.
Someone still keeps this place. The approach has been cleared of cover for a bowshot in every direction, and you are standing in the middle of it.
A dry moat, a lowered bridge, and a door standing open just wide enough to be an invitation.
origins: a border keep that changed hands three times
a customs house fortified past all reason
a garrison built to watch something that is still there

dungeonKinds.label: Desecrated temple
approaches: Steps climb to a portico where the god's name has been chiselled out of every inscription, patiently, one letter at a time.
The doors are bronze and green with age, and they are ajar. Offerings rot on the step, left recently by someone who did not go inside.
A processional way runs straight to the entrance, paved and swept clean. Someone still walks it.
motifs: prayer strips in a dead script
origins: a shrine rededicated by force
a cathedral built over an older, worse altar
a hermitage that answered the wrong prayer

dungeonKinds.label: Delve / mine
approaches: The adit is timbered and the timbers are sound, which is the first surprise. The second is that the rails running out of it are clean of rust.
Spoil heaps grey the whole hillside. The tunnel mouth breathes cold air, and somewhere below it, water is moving.
A winch stands over the shaft with its rope run out to the very end. Whatever it lowered last, it has not brought back up.
origins: a shaft sunk chasing a seam that turned into something else
a company mine abandoned after the third collapse
a delve that broke into a room nobody dug

dungeonKinds.label: Wreck
approaches: The hull lies canted on the rocks with its ribs open to the weather. The tide has been in and out of it a thousand times and left the inside dark.
Rigging trails in the water like weed. A boarding plank has been laid across recently, by someone who is either still aboard or is not.
Gulls stand along the rail and do not trouble to fly as you approach, which says something about how long they have had the place to themselves.
origins: a trader driven onto the rocks with its cargo intact
a warship that sank at anchor with no survivors
a hull that washed up already empty

dungeonKinds.label: Planar pocket
approaches: The doorway stands with no building around it, and the light coming through it is the wrong colour for this afternoon.
There is a seam in the air ahead. Sound arrives late from the other side of it, and arrives wrong.
Grass grows up to a line and stops. Past that line the ground belongs to somewhere else.
motifs: a smell of copper and cut grass
origins: a bubble of somewhere else pressed into a hillside
a house that only has an inside
a stair that goes down further than the hill is tall

dungeonKinds.label: Megadungeon
approaches: The mouth is a stair wide enough for a cart, worn hollow down the middle by traffic that stopped centuries ago.
Whatever this place is, the entrance is only its collar. Cold air pours steadily out of it, out of a volume you cannot begin to guess at.
Camps ring the entrance, abandoned at different times and in different styles. Everyone comes here. Not everyone comes back.
motifs: cold air moving from somewhere below
materials: layered construction from three different centuries
origins: a city that was buried on purpose
a vault complex that outgrew its purpose
a shaft that was a temple, then a prison, then a mine

threshold: The way in: {material} steps down under a lintel carved with a warning in a script three centuries out of use. {motif} has drifted into the corners.
A doorway of {material}, propped open with a wedge somebody drove in recently. The air coming out is colder than the air going in.
The entrance hall stands open to the sky where the roof fell. {motif} lies over everything in an even layer, and there are fresh tracks through it.
junction: {passages} passages meet under a sagging arch of {material}. Someone has scratched tally marks at eye height on every one.
A landing where the stair turns. Drips from above have cut a channel through {motif} on the floor.
A wide corridor of {material} with alcoves down both sides, all of them empty, all of them the right size for a person.
encounter: A long room of {material}. Furniture has been dragged into a rough barricade at the far end and abandoned there.
A vaulted chamber where {motif} has been swept into piles, as if something tidy lives here.
The floor here is a foot deep in cold water. Whatever is in the room is standing in it, comfortably.
A hall with a gallery running around it at half height. Good ground for the things already up there.
puzzle: A room built to be worked out rather than walked through: the {material} dressed flat, the {motif} repeated at every turn, and something at the centre of it that expects to be handled.
The chamber is in better repair than anything around it. Whatever it was made to do, the builders meant it to still be doing it.
A bare room, and deliberately so, so that the one thing standing in it cannot be overlooked.
Nothing here was made for comfort. Every surface is a working surface, and the {motif} above them reads as instructions to somebody.
The dust lies thick and undisturbed, except in the few places this room expects to be touched.
trap: A stretch of {material} the builders took more care over than the rooms on either side of it.
An unremarkable room, which is itself worth remarking on: everything of interest here is at floor and ceiling rather than on the walls.
There is no wear down the middle of this floor, the way there is everywhere else. Nothing has walked here in a long time.
A plain chamber with an unusually clear line of sight end to end, and no cover anywhere in it.
Old scorch, old stains, and a great deal of undisturbed dust. This room has been used, and not for living in.
treasure: A strongroom, its door already forced. Whoever opened it took the obvious things and missed the rest.
A collapsed store-chamber where {motif} half-buries crates stamped with a merchant house that no longer exists.
A shrine-niche where offerings were left and never collected, decades of them.
lore: Wall paintings in flaking pigment run the length of the room, telling a story that stops abruptly two thirds along.
A records room. Damp has taken most of it, but not all, and the surviving pages are the interesting ones.
Someone died here writing on the wall in charcoal, and got fifteen words down.
empty: An empty chamber of {material}. Cold, quiet, and the only sound is water somewhere below.
A store-room stripped to the shelves. {motif} on the floor is undisturbed.
Living quarters, long abandoned. Bedding rotted to fibre, a cup, a boot, nothing worth carrying.
A hall too big for its purpose, echoing, with nothing in it at all.
haven: A barred side-chamber with a spring, a cold hearth, and signs of recent, careful occupation.
A cell that locks from the inside, which is the point.
A high gallery, defensible, with a view of the approach and someone already in it.
shortcut: A collapsed wall opens onto a passage that runs back toward the entrance, once you clear it from this side.
A winch-lift, still rigged, that can be brought up but only from here.
A barred door with the bar on this side, opening straight onto the approach road.
boss: The chamber the whole place was built around: {material} rising to a vault, {motif} in drifts against the walls, and a floor kept deliberately clear.
A flooded rotunda with a raised dais at its centre, and everything in the room angled to face it.
A hall of {material} pillars, half of them broken, arranged so that anyone entering is seen long before they see.

dressings: A cold draught moves through steadily; something further in is open to the air.
The walls are damp to the touch and the damp is warm.
Every surface at knee height has been rubbed smooth by decades of passing traffic.
There are tallies scratched by the door, and the count reaches four hundred and stops.
Somewhere below, at irregular intervals, something heavy is set down.
The dust here has been disturbed within the last day.
A smell of old smoke that has nothing to burn.
The light behaves oddly at the edges of the room, arriving a half-second late.
Rats have made a road through here and will not use one particular corner.
Old bloodstains, scrubbed at, not successfully.

hallwayTypes.name: Pillared
hallwayTypes.desc: Rows of squat stone columns line both sides, close enough to break up a charge and to hide a body.

hallwayTypes.name: Rough-hewn
hallwayTypes.desc: The passage is unfinished cave rock, the tool marks of whoever widened it still on the walls.

hallwayTypes.name: Ankle-deep water
hallwayTypes.desc: Standing water covers the floor to the shin. Every step is heard twice.

hallwayTypes.name: Part collapsed
hallwayTypes.desc: A fall of rubble narrows the way to a crawl; squeezing through costs half speed.

hallwayTypes.name: Gothic arches
hallwayTypes.desc: Tall pointed arches repeat the length of it, each one a little out of true with the last.

hallwayTypes.name: Sconced
hallwayTypes.desc: Iron sconces every few paces, half of them still burning. Someone tends them.

hallwayTypes.name: Lightless
hallwayTypes.desc: No sconce, no shaft, no glow. Whatever lives here does not need to see.

hallwayTypes.name: Grated floor
hallwayTypes.desc: Iron grating underfoot, with a drop below it you cannot see the bottom of.

hallwayTypes.name: Chasm span
hallwayTypes.desc: The floor gives out and a narrow ledge crosses the gap. Below is a long fall.

hallwayTypes.name: Rope bridge
hallwayTypes.desc: Plank and rope, swaying, with two boards missing near the middle.

hallwayTypes.name: Ice-slicked
hallwayTypes.desc: The stone is glazed with ice. Moving faster than a walk asks for a saving throw.

hallwayTypes.name: Overgrown
hallwayTypes.desc: Roots have come through the ceiling and vines have taken the walls back.

hallwayTypes.name: Fungal
hallwayTypes.desc: Pale mushrooms grow thick along the base of the walls and give off a faint light.

hallwayTypes.name: Bone-lined
hallwayTypes.desc: Skulls and long bones stacked shoulder-high on both sides, sorted by kind.

hallwayTypes.name: Catacomb niches
hallwayTypes.desc: Recessed alcoves at head height, each holding a shrouded body.

hallwayTypes.name: Stacked shelves
hallwayTypes.desc: Bookshelves form the walls themselves, the volumes swollen with damp.

hallwayTypes.name: Weapon racks
hallwayTypes.desc: Racks and armour stands the whole length, most of them empty.

hallwayTypes.name: Statue gallery
hallwayTypes.desc: Carved figures on pedestals, all of them facing the way you came in.

hallwayTypes.name: Portrait hall
hallwayTypes.desc: Framed faces the length of the wall. The eyes have been recut, recently.

hallwayTypes.name: Draped
hallwayTypes.desc: Heavy hangings cover the walls, and at least two of them cover something else.

hallwayTypes.name: Ceremonial approach
hallwayTypes.desc: Wide, and carpeted down the middle in a red that was once better kept.

hallwayTypes.name: Cell block
hallwayTypes.desc: Barred cells on both sides. Most stand open. One does not.

hallwayTypes.name: Sewer run
hallwayTypes.desc: A curved brick tunnel with a sludge channel down the middle and a ledge either side.

hallwayTypes.name: Timbered shaft
hallwayTypes.desc: Timber props every few feet and the rails of a cart track underfoot.

hallwayTypes.name: Stacked crates
hallwayTypes.desc: Crates and barrels stacked to the ceiling, leaving a path barely wide enough.

hallwayTypes.name: Branching
hallwayTypes.desc: It forks and forks again, and three of the four ways are a dozen feet of nothing.

hallwayTypes.name: Spiral ramp
hallwayTypes.desc: A continuous curving incline, so gradual you only notice the climb at the end.

hallwayTypes.name: Whispering
hallwayTypes.desc: The shape of it carries voices from somewhere else, always just below sense.

hallwayTypes.name: Blood-soaked
hallwayTypes.desc: Fresh gore and a drag mark leading away, still tacky.

hallwayTypes.name: Ported walls
hallwayTypes.desc: Small holes at knee and throat height, in pairs, the whole length of it.

passageTraps.name: Tripline and falling block

passageTraps.effect: 3d10 bludgeoning, DC 14 Dexterity for half, and the passage is blocked until the block is levered clear

passageTraps.name: Dart slots

passageTraps.effect: two darts, +6 to hit, 1d4 piercing plus 2d6 poison each

passageTraps.effect: a 20 ft drop for 2d6 bludgeoning, and the lid shuts overhead

passageTraps.name: Scything blade in the arch
passageTraps.telegraph: a clean groove in both walls at hip height

passageTraps.name: Alarm wire
passageTraps.telegraph: a taut hair-thin wire an inch above the floor
passageTraps.effect: no damage; a bell rings somewhere ahead and the site becomes alert

passageTraps.name: Flame jet

passageTraps.disarm: DC 15 Thieves' Tools, or shut the valve found upstream
passageTraps.effect: 4d6 fire, DC 14 Dexterity for half, to everything in a 10 ft length of the passage

passageTraps.name: Collapsing shoring

passageTraps.disarm: DC 14 Strength to prop it properly first
passageTraps.effect: 3d6 bludgeoning, DC 13 Dexterity for half, and the passage is closed until it is dug out

passageTraps.name: Greased slope and spikes

passageTraps.disarm: sand or ash along the length of it
passageTraps.effect: DC 13 Dexterity or slide to the bottom for 2d6 piercing

traps.name: Scything blade
traps.telegraph: a clean horizontal groove in both walls at hip height
traps.effect: 2d10 slashing, DC 14 Dexterity save for half
traps.consequence: the mechanism resets audibly, and everything nearby now knows where you are

traps.name: Collapsing floor
traps.disarm: DC 15 Thieves' Tools or simply spanning it
traps.effect: a 20 ft drop, 2d6 bludgeoning, DC 13 Dexterity save to catch the lip
traps.consequence: whoever falls is separated from the party and lands somewhere with its own occupants

traps.name: Poison needle lock
traps.telegraph: a keyhole with a bright, un-tarnished rim
traps.effect: 1 piercing plus 3d6 poison, DC 15 Constitution save for half
traps.consequence: the poisoned character has disadvantage on the next long stretch until treated

traps.name: Sealing door and rising water
traps.telegraph: a drain grate and a waterline stained a foot up the wall
traps.disarm: DC 16 Strength to hold the door, or find the sluice
traps.effect: the room floods over six rounds
traps.consequence: gear is soaked, torches are out, and the next room is entered wet and cold

traps.name: Glyph of alarm and binding
traps.telegraph: a faint scorch outline on the threshold
traps.effect: DC 14 Wisdom save or restrained for 1 minute
traps.consequence: the alarm carries, and reinforcements arrive in 1d4 rounds

traps.name: Falling portcullis and murder holes
traps.telegraph: a slot in the ceiling and holes above the corridor
traps.disarm: DC 14 Thieves' Tools on the counterweight
traps.effect: the party is split, and 1d4 attackers fire from above
traps.consequence: the split lasts until the winch is found, two rooms away

traps.name: Crushing walls

traps.disarm: DC 16 Thieves' Tools, or jam it with something solid
traps.effect: 4d10 bludgeoning over three rounds unless stopped
traps.consequence: whatever is used to jam it is destroyed

traps.name: Spore bloom

traps.effect: DC 13 Constitution save or poisoned for 1 hour
traps.consequence: the poisoned condition makes the next social encounter noticeably harder

puzzles.name: The order of the seasons
puzzles.premise: Four reliefs must be turned to show the seasons in the order this place used, which is not the order anyone uses now.
puzzles.solution: the mural in the lore room shows the old calendar starting at first frost
puzzles.alternate: DC 16 History, or DC 18 Thieves' Tools to force the mechanism
puzzles.failure: the mechanism jams for an hour and something is alerted

puzzles.name: The weighed name
puzzles.premise: A scale, a set of lead letters, and a door that opens when the correct name is weighed out.
puzzles.solution: the name is written on the founder's coffin plate elsewhere in the site
puzzles.alternate: DC 15 Investigation on the discarded letters to work out what is missing
puzzles.failure: the wrong weight drops the counterweight and seals the room for ten minutes

puzzles.name: Nine spouts, one basin
puzzles.premise: Nine valves, one basin, and only one combination fills it before it drains.
puzzles.solution: the drain rate is written on the pipework in a maintenance hand
puzzles.alternate: DC 16 Arcana to freeze the drain, or plug it with anything
puzzles.failure: the overflow floods the corridor behind them

puzzles.name: The unlit lamp
puzzles.premise: Eleven lamps, ten already burning, and a door that will not open while any of them is lit by ordinary fire.
puzzles.solution: the eleventh must be lit with light rather than flame, and then all of them snuffed at once
puzzles.alternate: DC 15 Arcana, or a well-argued use of any light cantrip
puzzles.failure: the lamps relight themselves and the room grows warmer each attempt

puzzles.name: The false inventory
puzzles.premise: A ledger lists twelve items stored here. Eleven are present. The door wants the twelfth.
puzzles.solution: the twelfth was taken by a previous intruder whose body lies two rooms on
puzzles.alternate: DC 17 Investigation to identify the substitution and forge it
puzzles.failure: the room's guardian is roused, having been listed as item twelve

puzzles.name: The echoed word
puzzles.premise: A word must be spoken here that was last spoken here, and the room remembers.
puzzles.solution: the word is recoverable from the charcoal writing left by the dying scribe
puzzles.alternate: DC 16 Perception to hear the room still whispering it
puzzles.failure: the room answers with its own word, and everyone who hears it takes 2d6 psychic damage

hazards: The floor of this section is rotten through; treat it as difficult terrain and roll for a drop each time a fight moves across it.

Standing water conducts what is in it; lightning and cold effects have their radius doubled here.

The growth on the walls reacts to light and closes passages behind a lit torch.

downtime.summary: Weeks pass. The party heals, spends, trains and repairs, and the world does not wait for them.
downtime.scene: For the first time since this began, there is nothing that has to be done today. The wounded stop being wounded, the coin gets spent, and {hub} goes about its business around you as though the country were not coming apart forty miles away.
downtime.goal: Spend the season well: heal, train, build what you will need, and shore up whoever is going to matter later.
activities: Recuperate: a full week of rest ends one long-term condition or a level of exhaustion.
Train: a month and 250 gp buys a language, a tool proficiency, or a hard-won knack the DM approves.
Craft: half the market cost in materials, 5 gp of progress per day, more with helpers.
Research: a week in the right archive answers one specific question about {villain} or the {objects}.
Work a trade: a week of honest labour covers modest lifestyle and earns a contact.
Carouse: a week of it makes one friend and one enemy, both of whom turn up later.
Repair standing: a week spent on {faction} moves their attitude one step.
complications: A letter arrives that nobody will admit to sending.
Somebody the party rescued turns up needing a place to stay, and knows something.
A price the party thought was settled is quietly raised.
Two of the party's allies fall out, publicly, and both want backing.
A rumour spreads that the party has already failed, and {hub} starts acting on it.
downtime.worldMoves: While the party rests, advance every clock one segment and let {villain} take one item off their schedule. Say what changed out loud at the end of the interlude.

missionBoard.summary: A pool of small jobs the party can take in any order, or skip entirely. Each pays, each teaches something, and one of them is not what it looks like.
missionBoard.scene: The notice board outside the hall is three layers deep in paper, and the tavern keeper is taking messages for people who cannot write. None of it is the war you came for. All of it is somebody's whole world.
missionBoard.goal: Pick up work, get paid, get known, and find out which of these jobs is connected to the thing you are actually chasing.

jobs.twist: the dead one was carrying a token from {villain}'s organisation

missionBoard.note: Three or four of these fill an evening. The one with a connection to the main plot is the DM's pick; the rest can stay ordinary.

siege.summary: A settlement the party cares about is attacked while they are inside it. There is no dungeon to leave for; the map is the walls.
siege.scene: The bell starts before dawn and does not stop. By the time you reach the wall there is enough light to count them, and counting them does not help. Whatever else happens today, the road out is closed.
siege.goal: Hold {place}, or get everyone out alive. Decide which of those you are doing before the second assault, because you cannot do both.
phases: Preparation: a few hours, and fewer resources than the plan needs. Every task assigned is a task not done elsewhere.
The probe: a small attack that tests the weakest point and withdraws, having learned it.
The night assault: aimed at morale, not walls. Fires, noise, and one real breach somewhere quiet.
The breach: the wall comes down where the party is not, and the fight is in the streets.
The morning: whoever is left counts the cost, and the survivors decide what they think of the party.
assignments: The gate: the obvious place, held by people who know they are the obvious place.
The weak wall: everyone knows which stretch it is; nobody has had the money to fix it.
The granary: lose it and the siege ends by starvation instead of assault.
The infirmary: undefended, full, and one street from the breach.
The evacuation route: only usable if somebody holds the far end of it.
siege.note: Split the party across assignments and cut between them. Whoever they did not go with is where the story happens.

heist.summary: Something the party needs is behind other people's walls. Casing, planning, execution, and the part of the plan that was always going to fail.
heist.scene: You can see it from the street: the place is not a fortress, which is somehow worse. Fortresses have one way in and a hundred guards. This has forty ways in and every single one of them is watched by somebody who is bored, well paid, and very awake.
heist.goal: Get in, take it, and get out without your faces becoming the story.
phases: Casing: three ways in, each with a different cost. Every hour spent looking is an hour the target has to move.
The plan: what they know, what they cannot know, and who has to be somewhere they should not be.
Execution: the one thing that is not where the plan says it is.
The exit: which is the actual problem, and where the plan has to be abandoned.

waysIn.cost: a forged writ, and somebody has to stand there while it is read
climbing gear, a distraction, and no way to carry anything heavy out
slow, filthy, and shared with something that lives there
somebody on the inside, which means somebody who can inform
a narrow window and no control over when it opens

complications: The thing has already been moved once and the party's information is a day old.
Somebody else is robbing the same place tonight.
A guard recognises one of the party from an earlier chapter.
What they came for is not alone in the vault, and the other thing is watching.
Getting it out means leaving somebody behind for an hour.

dilemmas.situation: Two groups are about to be lost at the same moment, in different places, and the party can reach one.

optionA.label: Save the many
optionA.cost: The one you leave is somebody with a name the party already knows.

optionB.label: Save the one
optionB.cost: A settlement loses a dozen people and knows exactly who chose not to come.

dilemmas.noGoodAnswer: There is no third option that saves both, and any plan to try costs the party the rest of the night.
dilemmas.later: Whoever survives turns up again later, either grateful and useful or bitter and talking.

dilemmas.situation: The quickest way through costs something the party swore not to spend: using {object} the way {villain} would use it.

optionA.label: Use it
optionA.cost: It works, and {villain}'s methods are now demonstrably the party's methods too.

optionB.label: Refuse
optionB.cost: The long way costs a week, and the clock does not pause for principle.

dilemmas.noGoodAnswer: Nobody who matters will ever know except the party, which is the whole point.
dilemmas.later: If they used it, an NPC who trusted them notices the change and says so in front of others.

dilemmas.situation: A lieutenant is beaten and asking for terms, and they know things no interrogation would get out of a corpse.

optionA.label: Take the deal
optionA.cost: They walk, they warn people, and someone the party protects pays for it.

optionB.label: Finish it
optionB.cost: The information dies with them, and the next chapter is walked into blind.

dilemmas.noGoodAnswer: Holding them prisoner requires somebody to guard them, and the party has nobody to spare.
dilemmas.later: A spared lieutenant reappears at the climax, on one side or the other depending on how the terms were honoured.

dilemmas.situation: The proof that would convict {villain} would also ruin people who only signed because they were desperate.

optionA.label: Use all of it
optionA.cost: The case is airtight and a dozen ordinary families are destroyed with it.

optionB.label: Use only the clean part
optionB.cost: The case has a hole, and {villain}'s people will find it.

dilemmas.noGoodAnswer: There is no way to separate the two halves that a hostile reader will accept.
dilemmas.later: {faction} takes a position on what the party chose, and acts on it.

dilemmas.situation: Someone with no love for {villain} will open the way, for a price the party would rather not pay in public.

optionA.label: Pay
optionA.cost: The road opens and the party is now publicly in business with them.

optionB.label: Refuse and force it
optionB.cost: It can be taken by force, loudly, and everything downstream is now alert.

dilemmas.noGoodAnswer: There is no quiet third road, and waiting is its own choice.
dilemmas.later: Whoever was paid, or fought, remembers it when the party needs them at the end.

dilemmas.situation: The only witness will testify, but only if the party gives up the thing they came here for.

optionA.label: Trade it away
optionA.cost: The objective stays in enemy hands one chapter longer than it had to.

optionB.label: Keep it
optionB.cost: The witness recants, and the truth becomes a rumour again.

dilemmas.noGoodAnswer: The witness is not bluffing and cannot be talked past; they have already lost too much.
dilemmas.later: The choice decides whether the finale can be won in public or only in private.

dilemmas.situation: A settlement in the way can be emptied or defended, and there is time for exactly one.

optionA.label: Evacuate
optionA.cost: Everyone lives and the place is lost, along with the supplies the party needed from it.

optionB.label: Hold
optionB.cost: The place stands if the party is lucky, and the butcher's bill is read out either way.

dilemmas.noGoodAnswer: The people themselves are split, loudly, and will hold the party to whichever they chose.
dilemmas.later: A held town becomes a base; an evacuated one becomes a column of refugees the party keeps meeting.

dilemmas.situation: Someone the party owes asks them to look away from something the party came here to stop.

optionA.label: Honour the debt
optionA.cost: The thing happens, and the party watched it happen.

optionB.label: Break it
optionB.cost: The debt-holder becomes an enemy who knows the party well.

dilemmas.noGoodAnswer: The ask is small, reasonable, and exactly the kind of thing that adds up.
dilemmas.later: The debt-holder either opens a door at the worst moment or closes one.

dilemmaFraming: Put it in front of the party while something else is still burning, so the clock is part of the choice.
Let both sides be argued by people the party likes. Nobody in this scene is a villain.
Do not offer a compromise. If the players invent a clever third path, make it cost a resource they will miss later.
Ask each player where their character stands before the group settles it; the split matters more than the answer.

rivalKinds.label: a rival free company
rivalKinds.wants: the same {objects} the party is chasing, to sell to the highest bidder
rivalKinds.method: moving fast, paying for information, and arriving first
rivalKinds.crosses: {villain} wants the {objects} used; the company wants them sold, and a sold {object} is one {villain} has to buy back
rivalKinds.offers: muscle, a second front, and everything they have already scouted
rivalKinds.demands: a cut, and first claim on the next {object} found
rivalKinds.ifAllied: Two crews can cover twice the ground: one optional chapter can be handled offscreen by the company, at the cost of whatever they keep from it.
rivalKinds.ifCrossed: They sell the party's route and timing to {villain}, who is waiting at the next site.
rivalKinds.leverage: They work for money, and {villain} has more of it. Outbid them once and they stay bought.

rivalKinds.label: a crown investigator
rivalKinds.wants: {villain} taken alive and tried, with the {objects} entered as evidence
rivalKinds.method: warrants, subpoenas, and the patient accumulation of testimony
rivalKinds.crosses: {villain} can survive a trial. A trial takes months, and the clock does not stop for procedure
rivalKinds.offers: legal cover, access to sealed records, and the authority to open doors
rivalKinds.demands: that nothing be destroyed and nobody be killed who could testify
rivalKinds.ifAllied: Charges stick. The ending shifts toward a public, permanent resolution rather than a body in a hole.
rivalKinds.ifCrossed: The party are the ones with warrants out, and every settlement becomes harder to work in.
rivalKinds.leverage: They must follow their own rules. Hand them a procedural excuse and they will act on it.

rivalKinds.label: a militant order
rivalKinds.wants: the same thing the party wants, and is willing to burn {region} down to get it
rivalKinds.method: purges, cordons, and the removal of anything that might be tainted
rivalKinds.crosses: {villain}'s plan dies with the region, and the order is entirely willing to trade one for the other
rivalKinds.offers: zealots who do not break, and the only people who will walk into the worst places
rivalKinds.demands: that the party stand aside from what comes after the victory
rivalKinds.ifAllied: The villain falls faster and harder, and the epilogue is uglier: the order keeps what it takes.
rivalKinds.ifCrossed: They add the party to the list of things to be cleansed, and they are thorough.
rivalKinds.leverage: Their doctrine is written down. Show them a reading of it that binds their hands.

rivalKinds.label: the antagonist's former partner
rivalKinds.wants: {villain} to suffer, personally, and does not much care what it costs {region}
rivalKinds.method: knowing exactly where {villain} is weak and spending other people to prove it
rivalKinds.crosses: they know the plan from the inside, which makes them the most useful and most dangerous person in the story
rivalKinds.offers: the truth about {villain}: the weakness, the schedule, the names
rivalKinds.demands: to be there at the end, and to be the one who does it
rivalKinds.ifAllied: The party skips a whole layer of investigation, and inherits a partner who will not stop when they should.
rivalKinds.ifCrossed: They go it alone, force the confrontation early, and lose, handing {villain} a warning.
rivalKinds.leverage: They want witnesses more than they want to win. Offer an audience.

rivalKinds.label: a profiteering house
rivalKinds.wants: the crisis to continue exactly long enough to corner the market it created
rivalKinds.method: buying scarcity, financing both sides, and owning the roads
rivalKinds.crosses: {villain} winning ends the crisis, and an ended crisis is an ended profit
rivalKinds.offers: money, supply, transport, and doors into rooms the party cannot afford
rivalKinds.demands: that certain routes stay closed and certain rivals stay ruined
rivalKinds.ifAllied: The party is never short of resources, and every settlement they save ends up owing the house.
rivalKinds.ifCrossed: Prices double, doors close, and a bounty appears that nobody will admit to funding.
rivalKinds.leverage: Show them a ledger where the villain's victory costs more than the party's does.

rivalKinds.label: a rival claimant
rivalKinds.wants: what {villain} wants, and by the same right, only sooner
rivalKinds.method: assembling a legitimate-looking case and an illegitimate army behind it
rivalKinds.crosses: there is one prize and two claims on it; both cannot be satisfied
rivalKinds.offers: troops, a banner to fight under, and a legitimate face for whatever the party does
rivalKinds.demands: that the party's victory install them at the end of it
rivalKinds.ifAllied: The finale has an army in it, and the region wakes up under a new power the party chose.
rivalKinds.ifCrossed: They cut a deal with {villain} instead, and the last chapter has two enemies in it.
rivalKinds.leverage: Their claim depends on being seen as the better option. Make that publicly untrue.

rivalKinds.label: an obsessive collector
rivalKinds.wants: the {objects} preserved and locked away, unused, forever
rivalKinds.method: buying, stealing, and occasionally entombing the people who used them
rivalKinds.crosses: {villain} intends to use the {objects}, which to the collector is a kind of murder
rivalKinds.offers: identification, history, and the one fact about the {objects} nobody else knows
rivalKinds.demands: every {object}, afterwards, with no exceptions and no copies
rivalKinds.ifAllied: The party learns what the {objects} really are, and hands away the only thing that could stop a sequel.
rivalKinds.ifCrossed: The collector reaches the next {object} first and it is simply gone, vault-sealed, unreachable.
rivalKinds.leverage: Offer them something rarer. There is always something rarer.

rivalKinds.label: an opportunist warlord
rivalKinds.wants: the territory everyone else is too distracted to hold
rivalKinds.method: taking undefended ground and daring anyone to come and get it
rivalKinds.crosses: {villain} needs {region} intact to use it; the warlord is busy eating it
rivalKinds.offers: an army, a border nobody can cross, and a very simple kind of help
rivalKinds.demands: the land they have taken, permanently, and no questions about how
rivalKinds.ifAllied: The map is safer and smaller: the party gains a wall at their back and loses the people behind it.
rivalKinds.ifCrossed: A second war opens across the party's supply line at the worst possible moment.
rivalKinds.leverage: They fear being caught between two forces. Show them the other jaw closing.

rivalMoves: They are already here. Fresh tracks, cut ropes, and a door opened by someone who knew the trick to it.
They arrive midway through, from another direction, and the party has a few rounds to decide whether that is good news.
They have taken a prisoner the party wanted, and will trade for something the party cannot spare.
They left a message scratched where the party would find it: a warning, an offer, or a boast, depending on how the last meeting went.
They have cleared the first third of the site and stopped, because what they found convinced them to wait for someone else to go first.
One of theirs is here alone, hurt, and separated from the rest. What the party does about it is remembered.
They got what they came for an hour ago and are on their way out. The party can let them pass, follow, or stop them.
They are negotiating with the occupants when the party walks in, and both sides turn around.
rivalFirstMeetings: Not in a fight: the party and {rival} reach for the same door, the same witness, or the same body at the same moment, and both stop.
Over a table in {hub}, arranged by someone who thought the two of them should talk before they cost each other anything.
Badly. Somebody drew, nobody died, and now there is a debt on one side of it.
As rescuers. {rival}'s people pull the party out of something, and make sure the party knows the price is not settled.
Through their reputation first: three chapters of the party finding {rival} was there yesterday, before ever seeing their face.

rivalStances.label: Hostile
rivalStances.note: They act against the party directly. Expect them at sites, in the way, and eventually in the climax on the wrong side.

rivalStances.label: Wary
rivalStances.note: The default. Neither side will spend blood on the other yet, and both are counting.

rivalStances.label: Allied
rivalStances.note: They fight alongside the party, and they will collect on what they are owed at the end.

reversals.label: The patron is bought
reversals.setup: {npc} has paid, vouched, and opened doors since the first week, and every road the party has taken was one {npc} suggested.
reversals.turn: {npc} has been reporting to {villain} the whole time. Not from malice: they were given a choice a year ago and took the only one that kept somebody alive.
foreshadow: {npc} knows a detail about a site the party has not told anybody about yet.
A message reaches {villain}'s people faster than the party travelled, twice.
{npc} steers the party away from one specific name, smoothly, more than once.
reversals.fallout: Everything the party told {npc} is already known. Every plan made in that room needs remaking, and {npc} is still the best-placed person to help, if they can be trusted with anything at all.
reversals.ifMissed: If the party never work it out, {npc} sells them the location of the finale, and the last chapter starts with an ambush instead of an approach.

reversals.label: The objective is the trap
reversals.setup: The {objects} have been the point of everything: find them, hold them, keep them from {villain}.
reversals.turn: Gathering them in one place is the last step of {villain}'s work, and the party has been doing it for them. Separated, the {objects} were inert. Together, they are the door.
foreshadow: Resistance at the second site was thinner than it should have been.
Something in {villain}'s own records refers to the party's route approvingly.
A dying servant of {villain} laughs when told what the party is carrying.
reversals.fallout: The party now has to decide whether to scatter what they spent the campaign gathering, and every ally who helped them gather it has an opinion.
reversals.ifMissed: If they bring the {objects} together as planned, the finale begins with {villain} thanking them, sincerely, in front of witnesses.

reversals.label: The villain was holding it back
reversals.setup: {villain} has been the cause of everything: the deaths, the clocks, the ruined country.
reversals.turn: {villain} is the last thing standing between {region} and what is actually underneath it. Their methods are indefensible; their reasoning is not.
foreshadow: {villain}'s people are dying in numbers that make no sense for a plan that is going well.
Something the party breaks makes the surrounding country worse, immediately and measurably.
A captured lieutenant asks, genuinely, whether the party has any idea what they are doing.
reversals.fallout: Beating {villain} is still possible and still might be right. It just no longer ends the campaign, and the party has to decide what does.
reversals.ifMissed: If the party kill {villain} without learning this, the ending arrives anyway, on the last page, in the form of what comes up next.

reversals.label: The one who was helping
reversals.setup: {npc} has fought beside the party, taken wounds for them, and asked for nothing that seemed unreasonable.
reversals.turn: {npc} wanted the party to succeed exactly this far and no further, and the moment they chose is the one where the party is most committed and least able to turn around.
foreshadow: {npc} is unusually insistent about the order in which things are done.
Somebody who knew {npc} before reacts badly to the name and will not explain.
{npc} asks a question about the party's plans that only matters if the answer is going somewhere.
reversals.fallout: The party is short one pair of hands at the worst time and long one enemy who knows their habits, their reserves, and how they fight.
reversals.ifMissed: There is nothing to miss. This one happens to the party rather than being deduced, which is why the foreshadowing matters.

reversals.label: Not dead, and not sorry
reversals.setup: Somebody was lost early: taken, drowned, buried, written off with a name on a list.
reversals.turn: They are alive and with {villain}, and they were not coerced. What they were offered, the party could not have matched.
foreshadow: A body was never actually produced, only reported.
Somebody on the other side fights like a person the party has trained with.
A personal item turns up in a place it could only have been carried to.
reversals.fallout: Every assumption about who talks to whom is wrong, and the party has to decide whether this is a rescue or a reckoning.
reversals.ifMissed: They reveal themselves at the finale, at the moment the party most needs one more ally and are counting heads.

reversals.label: The rival read it correctly
reversals.setup: {rival} has been an obstacle, a competitor, and an irritant, and their account of the situation was self-serving nonsense.
reversals.turn: Their account was accurate. They were the only people who understood the shape of this, which is why they behaved the way they did.
foreshadow: {rival} declines an opportunity that would obviously profit them, and will not say why.
Their people are equipped for something the party has not encountered yet.
Something {rival} said in the first meeting turns out to have been a literal description.
reversals.fallout: The party has spent the campaign hindering the one group with the correct plan, and repairing that costs either pride or leverage.
reversals.ifMissed: If nobody catches on, {rival} carries out their plan without the party, succeeds partially, and the party arrives to a finished argument.

reversals.label: The victim wrote the whole thing
reversals.setup: {place} has been the wounded party throughout: raided, taxed, emptied, begging for help.
reversals.turn: {place}, or the people who run it, invited this. They needed a crisis, or a scapegoat, or the war itself, and {villain} was the instrument rather than the author.
foreshadow: The losses are always in the same quarter, and never the one that matters.
Somebody profits visibly and is never once suspected.
A record the party is shown has been very carefully curated.
reversals.fallout: Beating {villain} solves the symptom and leaves the cause running the town the party has been using as a base.
reversals.ifMissed: The party wins, is thanked publicly by the people who arranged it, and the epilogue is written by them.

reversals.label: The deadline is a lie
reversals.setup: Everyone agrees on how long there is. The whole plan is built on that number.
reversals.turn: The real deadline is much sooner, and the comfortable one was put about deliberately so that competent people would pace themselves.
foreshadow: Preparations on the other side are further along than the timetable allows.
Two sources give the same date in the same words, which is one source.
Somebody who should be panicking is not.
reversals.fallout: Every plan that depended on having time needs redoing now, and the party has to choose what to abandon.
reversals.ifMissed: The clock simply fills earlier than the party expected, and they arrive to find the work already done.

villainGains: {villain}'s people take the {object} from {place}. Whatever the party planned to do with it, they do it without.
The road through {place} is closed and held. Every journey in {region} is now two days longer and watched.
{npc} is dead. Not dramatically: they are simply not there the next time the party asks for them.
{faction} comes to terms with {villain}. Their doors, their people and their information close in the same afternoon.
{place} changes hands. The party's contacts there are now somebody else's contacts.
The party's approach to the finale is known and prepared for; the first encounter there begins with them surrounded.
{villain}'s lieutenant is promoted and given a free hand, and a second front opens behind the party.
A public account of events is circulated in which the party are the cause. Enough people believe it to matter.
villainMoves: sends a competent lieutenant to negotiate, honestly, once
takes something from {hub} that the party will notice
makes an example of a settlement that had nothing to do with it
accelerates the timetable and stops being careful
offers the party exactly what they want in exchange for one step back
removes the witness before the party can reach them

endings.label: Clean
endings.text: {villain} is stopped before the last segment fills. {region} keeps its shape, {hub} rebuilds, and the {objects} are accounted for.

endings.label: Costly
endings.text: {villain} is stopped, but the {objects} are spent doing it and {hub} pays a price that shows on the map.

endings.label: Bargained
endings.text: {villain} is not defeated but bound: the plan stops, the terms hold, and everyone involved has to live with the wording.

endings.label: Too Late
endings.text: The clock fills. {villain} succeeds, and the campaign continues in the world that makes: the party is now the only thing that knows how it happened.

endings.label: Inherited
endings.text: {villain} is destroyed and the vacancy is filled by something the party had been treating as an ally.

take one of them alive and leave the rest as a message
stop anyone reaching the far door, whatever it costs
recover what the party is carrying and withdraw
buy time for the ritual two rooms on
identify the party, then report back to {villain}
protect the thing in the corner that nobody has looked at yet
drive them back the way they came without killing anyone, if possible
encounterTactics: opens at range, falls back through prepared ground, forces the party to come to it
attacks the rearmost character first and tries to separate them
fights in the doorway where numbers do not help
waits until the party commits to the room, then closes the way out
targets whoever is holding a light source
one holds the front while the others work around through the side passage
does not fight fairly and has no interest in a standing battle
sacrifices the weakest of its number to set up a single decisive attack
encounterMorale: breaks at half strength and runs deeper in to warn the rest
will not break; it has been told what happens if it does
surrenders if offered anything at all, and will talk
fights to the last, then the survivor tries to take one of the party with it
withdraws in good order once its objective is impossible
breaks if its leader falls, and not before
encounterIfAvoided: these forces are somewhere else in the site later, and better positioned
the alarm goes up an hour later and the deeper rooms are ready
nothing immediately, but they are between the party and the way out on the way back
they carry word to {villain}, who moves {object}
they follow at a distance and pick a worse moment
the site simply gets quieter, and something notices the silence
havenOccupants: a handful of survivors from the last group who came in, out of food and out of nerve
a deserter from {villain}'s people who will trade the layout for safe passage
a rival crew who got here first, currently resting, currently reasonable
a scholar who has been living here for a month and does not want to be rescued yet
prisoners, locked in, who have heard everything through the wall
treasureGoods: a bundle of correspondence in {villain}'s hand, unsigned but distinctive
trade bars stamped with a house that will want to know where they came from
a map case holding surveys of three sites, one of them {next}
ceremonial gear worth a great deal to exactly one buyer
a strongbox of coin from a mint that closed sixty years ago
linkSummaries: What the party takes out of here names {next} plainly; the only question is how fast they move.
{next} is where the trail goes. Anyone who survives this place is already on the road there.
The work here was being done for somewhere else, and the paperwork says {next}.
Someone here was expected at {next} and is not going to make it. The party can go in their place.
The route to {next} is the thing worth carrying out of this chapter, and three separate people here know it.
objectiveNotes: Held in the deepest room, and its keeper knows exactly what it is.
Hidden in plain sight and mislabelled; the party will walk past it once.
Already being moved when the party arrives, which is the whole encounter.
In the hands of someone who will hand it over for a price the party will not like.
Sealed behind a lock that opens for one person, and that person is dead but not gone.
openings: Session one opens on the road into {hub}, late in the day, with the weather turning. The party shares the last miles with a carter who talks too much, and half of what he says about {region} turns out to matter. The gate is manned by too few people asking too many questions, and somewhere behind the party, out of sight, {villain}'s people are on the same road.

Start in the common room of the inn at {hub}, the night the news arrives. Let the players order drinks and introduce themselves before the door opens; whoever carries the news is bleeding, and what they say in front of the whole room is the campaign's first clue. Everyone hears it. Not everyone wants it heard.

Open mid-journey: the party has been travelling through {region} for three days on other business when they find the first sign that something is wrong, blocking the road where it cannot be ignored. {hub} is the nearest place with walls, beds, and answers, and by the time they reach it, word of what they found has somehow arrived first.

Begin with the job that was supposed to be simple: an escort, a delivery, a survey, paid for by {npc} and worth exactly enough to take. It goes wrong at the edge of {region} in a way that is clearly not an accident, and the survivors' road leads to {hub}.

Open on the aftermath: the party arrives at a place where {villain}'s people finished their work an hour ago. What is left tells them three things: what was taken, which way they went, and that whoever did it was not worried about being followed. {hub} is where the trail points.
characterHooks: One PC grew up in {hub} and still owes somebody there; the trouble threatens the person they owe.
One PC's family signed something generations back that {villain}'s plan touches directly. They find their own surname in the first chapter.
One PC came to {region} looking for a person who has gone missing, and the trail runs straight through the campaign's chapters.
One PC served with, apprenticed under, or was saved by {npc}, and it is {npc} who asks for help.
One PC has a professional interest, a commission from {faction}, a bounty, a scholarly grant, that the campaign keeps paying, until the price changes.
One PC has met {villain} before, years ago and under another name, and will be recognised.
One PC's god, order, or teacher sent them here with instructions that made no sense at the time and are starting to.
One PC is from {region} and left for a reason; the campaign is the reason, older and larger than they knew.
clockTriggers: the party spends a full week on downtime, rest, or unhurried travel
